planting.note: Direct sow seeds 1 inch deep in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun after soil is thoroughly warm; California Blackeye 5 was bred at UC Davis from a California Blackeye x Iron cross and carries resistance to root-knot nematode and cowpea (Fusarium) wilt, valuable traits for the sandy, nematode-prone soils common along the Gulf Coast.

directions: Direct sow seeds 1 inch deep in lean to moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the soil is thoroughly warm; California Blackeye 5 is an improved release from the University of California, Davis, bred from a cross of California Blackeye and the nematode-resistant Iron cowpea to combine the classic black-eyed pea's mild, earthy flavor with real genetic resistance to root-knot nematode and cowpea (Fusarium) wilt, two soil-borne problems that persist for years in garden soil and are especially common in sandy Gulf Coast ground. The semi-bush plants are more compact and manageable than old-fashioned vining types and need no staking. Harvest the fresh green pods as snap beans, pick the shelled green peas for fresh eating, or let pods dry fully on the vine for the classic dried black-eyed peas of Southern cooking. Like other Southern peas, it fixes nitrogen and improves soil fertility as it grows.
sources: University of California, Davis — Foundation Seed Program

common_name: Top Pick Pinkeye Southern Pea (Easy-Harvest Purple Hull Type)

planting.note: Direct sow seeds 1 inch deep in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun after soil is thoroughly warm; Top Pick Pinkeye is an improved open-pollinated pinkeye purple hull type bred to concentrate its pods at the top of the plant for faster, cleaner picking — a real time-saver during the peak of a Gulf South summer harvest.

directions: Direct sow seeds 1 inch deep in lean to moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the soil is thoroughly warm; Top Pick Pinkeye is an improved pinkeye purple hull southern pea bred so that pods set concentrated near the top of the plant rather than scattered throughout, letting a picker harvest a full basket quickly without hunting through foliage — a meaningful advantage during the heavy summer flush when Southern peas are at their most productive. The cream-colored peas with a distinctive pink eye have the classic mild, slightly sweet flavor prized in Southern cooking. Harvest pods when they've turned the characteristic purple-pink color and the peas inside have filled out but are still tender for fresh shelling, or let pods dry fully for storage. Like other Southern peas, the plant fixes nitrogen and improves soil fertility as it grows, and thrives in the long, hot Gulf South summer.
sources: seed catalog reference (Stokes Seeds, Rupp Seeds, Holmes Seed Company)

common_name: Bossa Nova Squash (Mottled Caserta-Type Virus-Resistant Zucchini)

planting.note: Direct sow 1 inch deep in hills after soil warms to 70°F; Bossa Nova is a 2015 All-America Selections winner with intermediate resistance to zucchini yellow mosaic virus and watermelon mosaic virus, along with an unusually long harvest window for a summer squash.

directions: Direct sow in warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger passes; Bossa Nova is a distinctive Caserta-type zucchini with striking dark and light green mottled skin, bred with intermediate resistance to zucchini yellow mosaic virus and watermelon mosaic virus, two viruses spread by aphids that commonly shorten a summer squash season in humid Gulf Coast gardens. It is also noted for an unusually extended harvest window compared to most zucchini, continuing to produce good-quality fruit later into the season. Pick fruit at 6-8 inches for the best texture and flavor, checking plants daily during peak production since squash left on the vine quickly grows oversized and seedy.
sources: All-America Selections — Bossa Nova squash AAS winner 2015
